searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase one — broad movie possibility space from one point of intent let many frames arise; the awtsmoos gives every vessel a different disguise. the protocol should describe meaning, not dictate renderer internals, so 2d and 3d can share time without sharing every implementation. movie language possibilities narrative films: casts, dialogue beats, blocking, gaze, expression, entrances, exits, reactions. tutorials: numbered steps, cursor/hand focus, arrows, highlights, zooms, labels, callouts, before/after states. infographics: bar, line, pie/donut, counters, timelines, progress rings, maps as shapes, comparison cards. motion graphics: text, rectangles, circles, polygons, paths, patches, masks, gradients, strokes, icons, grids. 3d scenes: cameras, perspective, lights, world objects, character/object transforms, fog/depth declarations. particles: sparks, snow, dust, confetti, fireflies, trails, bursts, star fields, data points. cinematography: wide, medium, closeup, extreme closeup, overhead, low/high angle, pov, orbit, dolly, truck, crane, rack focus intent. transitions: cut, crossfade, wipe, push, zoom, iris, match motion, dip, flash. animation: keyframes, easing, spring intent, loops, staggering, path motion, transform/opacity/style channels. audio metadata: dialogue/music/sfx cues and ducking intent, even when a renderer only preserves metadata. accessibility: safe title areas, caption semantics, contrast hints, reduced motion substitutions. formats: landscape, portrait, square, responsive preview, explicit fps/duration. five candidate architectures a — one giant renderer one engine draws everything. rejected: destroys mature app identities and duplicates specialist work. b — shared json protocol + capability adapters canonical movie document plus per app adapters. preferred: ai gets one language while each app advertises supported subsets. c — nesher as universal host everything becomes nle clips. useful for finishing, weak for semantic authoring and live procedural character control. d — animator as universal host everything becomes animator entities. strong cinematic path, but over couples simple motion graphics and editing workflows. e — event bus only apps exchange loose events. flexible but insufficiently deterministic for ai generation, validation, or durable movie files. preferred direction architecture b, with optional handoff into d for cinematic realization and c for finishing/export. captions remains a fast 2d composition pet; animator remains the director/world pet; nesher remains the editor/export pet. ideal end state an ai can inspect capabilities(), emit one schema valid document, preview it, hand scenes to the best renderer, preserve unsupported semantic layers for another app, and export or edit without reverse engineering private internals.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two critique — twenty improvements the awtsmoos hides no weakness from review; each critique makes the vessel more true. 1. require exact protocol versioning and forward compatible unknown metadata. 2. distinguish semantic layer kind from preferred renderer implementation. 3. make duration validation exact enough to prove 180 seconds. 4. require stable ids so ai retries do not create accidental duplicates. 5. add capability reports rather than pretending every app supports every primitive. 6. preserve unsupported layers during handoff instead of dropping them. 7. validate scene overlap/gaps intentionally rather than accidentally. 8. normalize transforms to explicit x/y/z, rotation, scale, anchor and opacity fields. 9. support both frame based and second based sampling through one clock. 10. keep easing deterministic and serializable. 11. separate chart data from chart visual style so ai can author factual structures cleanly. 12. separate character intent from low level rig channels. 13. separate camera intent from app specific camera math. 14. add safe area metadata for mobile captions and controls. 15. expose reduced motion substitutions for preview ui. 16. make adapter conversion return warnings and unsupported capabilities. 17. test first/middle/last frames and every scene boundary. 18. include recurring cast continuity across scenes in the showcase. 19. include mixed 2d over 3d overlays to prove compositing semantics. 20. keep every new source file below the repository's modular size target and split before compression. revised decision build a deliberately small core with no renderer dependency. the protocol is the shared language; adapters are translation boundaries; existing renderers remain authoritative for their specialty.
